text: RcppTrust::trust() drop-replacement trust::trust(). arguments, defaults, return value, implements exact algorithm: Newton / easy-easy / hard-easy / hard-hard case split trust-region subproblem, accept/reject radius-adjustment rule, termination criteria. Everything already know trust::trust() – objfun contract (return list value, gradient, hessian, list(value = Inf)/list(value = -Inf) signal infeasible point), rinit/rmax/parscale/iterlim/fterm/mterm/ minimize/blather arguments, shape returned list, blather = TRUE’s extra argpath/steptype/rho/… components – applies unchanged. 10 upstream’s tests/*.R scripts ported package’s test suite pass C++ core.
code: library(RcppTrust)  # Rosenbrock's function, exactly the example from ?trust::trust objfun <- function(x) {   f <- expression(100 * (x2 - x1^2)^2 + (1 - x1)^2)   g1 <- D(f, "x1"); g2 <- D(f, "x2")   h11 <- D(g1, "x1"); h12 <- D(g1, "x2"); h22 <- D(g2, "x2")   x1 <- x[1]; x2 <- x[2]   list(     value = eval(f), gradient = c(eval(g1), eval(g2)),     hessian = rbind(c(eval(h11), eval(h12)), c(eval(h12), eval(h22)))   ) }  out <- trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5) out[c("value", "argument", "converged", "iterations")] #> $value #> [1] 5.165437e-15 #>  #> $argument #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 21

code: library(microbenchmark)  # same Rosenbrock objfun as above: 2 parameters, ~20 iterations mb_small <- microbenchmark(   trust = trust::trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5),   RcppTrust = RcppTrust::trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5),   times = 50 ) print(mb_small) #> Unit: microseconds #>       expr      min       lq      mean   median       uq      max neval #>      trust 1313.688 1344.723 1547.2143 1372.976 1467.226 3613.313    50 #>  RcppTrust  589.188  610.941  639.2165  626.744  663.840  746.492    50 d <- 30 mu <- seq_len(d) barrier_objfun <- function(x) {   normxsq <- sum(x^2)   omnormxsq <- 1 - normxsq   if (normxsq >= 1) return(list(value = Inf))   f <- sum(x * mu) - log(omnormxsq)   g <- mu + 2 * x / omnormxsq   B <- 4 * outer(x, x) / omnormxsq^2 + 2 * diag(d) / omnormxsq   list(value = f, gradient = g, hessian = B) }  r1 <- trust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100) r2 <- RcppTrust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100) # same solution, different number of steps to get there (see above) c(trust_iterations = r1$iterations, RcppTrust_iterations = r2$iterations) #>     trust_iterations RcppTrust_iterations  #>                   16                   16 max(abs(r1$argument - r2$argument)) #> [1] 2.775558e-17  mb_large <- microbenchmark(   trust = trust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100),   RcppTrust = RcppTrust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100),   times = 30 ) print(mb_large) #> Unit: microseconds #>       expr      min       lq      mean   median       uq      max neval #>      trust 1896.997 1951.988 2246.5193 2013.034 2676.618 2752.671    30 #>  RcppTrust  683.969  744.890  833.4008  881.799  920.412  990.326    30

Instead – following header-, positionally-indexed function-pointer pattern already used across nlmixr2 ecosystem (rxode2, n1qn1, lbfgsb3c) – consumer resolves trust_solve_c/trust_result_free function pointers , load time. full wiring three pieces, example reproduces single self-contained file demonstration. Add RcppTrust DESCRIPTION’s LinkingTo (header) Imports (R-level .RcppTrustPtr() getter). one translation unit, include registration header package-unique renaming #define generated init function doesn’t collide consumer’s: package’s .onLoad(), resolve pointers : , trust_solve_c_ptr trust_result_free_ptr (, optimizers, steihaug_solve_c_ptr, bobyqa_solve_c_ptr, newuoa_solve_c_ptr *_free_ptr partners; see vignette("trust-region-methods")) live function pointers signatures trust_solve_c()/trust_result_free(), usable anywhere package’s C++ – including inside OpenMP loop fitting many subjects’ problems parallel: example whole pattern collapsed one file run live, via Rcpp::sourceCpp(), exactly work split across real package’s src/init.c, R/zzz.R, wherever fit happens: Note compiled file never links RcppTrust’s shared library – LinkingTo/Rcpp::depends() adds inst/include directory compiler’s include path. Every trust_* symbol used except two resolved pointers (trust_solve_c_ptr, trust_result_free_ptr) type macro, function call, exactly point: nothing creates ABI dependency specific build RcppTrust, stable, append-pointer table publishes.
code: extern "C" { #define iniRcppTrustPtrs _mypkg_iniRcppTrustPtrs #include <RcppTrust.h> iniRcppTrust } .onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {   .Call(`_mypkg_iniRcppTrustPtrs`, RcppTrust:::.RcppTrustPtr(), PACKAGE = "mypkg") } #pragma omp parallel for for (int i = 0; i < nSubjects; i++) {   trust_options_t opts = trust_options_default(1.0, 5.0);   trust_result_t res;   trust_solve_c_ptr(n, parinit[i], subject_objfun, &subjectData[i], &opts, &res);   // ... use res.argument, res.value, res.converged ...   trust_result_free_ptr(&res); } cpp_code <- ' // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppTrust)]] #include <Rcpp.h>  extern "C" { #define iniRcppTrustPtrs _vignette_iniRcppTrustPtrs #include <RcppTrust.h> iniRcppTrust }  // A thread-safe C objective function: Rosenbrock again, this time // filling value/gradient/hessian directly instead of returning a list. extern "C" int rosenbrock_c(int n, const double *par, double *value,                              double *gradient, double *hessian, void *ud) {   double x1 = par[0], x2 = par[1];   double t = x2 - x1 * x1;   *value = 100.0 * t * t + (1.0 - x1) * (1.0 - x1);   gradient[0] = -400.0 * x1 * t - 2.0 * (1.0 - x1);   gradient[1] = 200.0 * t;   hessian[0] = -400.0 * x2 + 1200.0 * x1 * x1 + 2.0;   hessian[1] = hessian[2] = -400.0 * x1;   hessian[3] = 200.0;   return 0; }  // [[Rcpp::export]] Rcpp::List fit_rosenbrock(SEXP ptrTable, Rcpp::NumericVector parinit) {   // normally done once, in .onLoad() -- see above   _vignette_iniRcppTrustPtrs(ptrTable);    trust_options_t opts = trust_options_default(1.0, 5.0);   trust_result_t res;   trust_solve_c_ptr(parinit.size(), parinit.begin(), rosenbrock_c, nullptr, &opts, &res);    Rcpp::List out = Rcpp::List::create(     Rcpp::_["argument"] = Rcpp::NumericVector(res.argument, res.argument + res.n),     Rcpp::_["value"] = res.value,     Rcpp::_["converged"] = res.converged != 0,     Rcpp::_["iterations"] = res.iterations);   trust_result_free_ptr(&res);   return out; } ' Rcpp::sourceCpp(code = cpp_code)  fit_rosenbrock(RcppTrust:::.RcppTrustPtr(), c(3, 1)) #> $argument #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $value #> [1] 5.165437e-15 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 21

title: More Trust-Region Methods: Steihaug, BOBYQA and NEWUOA
text: four repeat loop: build quadratic model objective, minimize within radius around current point, compare actual decrease predicted one, grow shrink radius. differ model comes subproblem solved. trust() uses exact gradient Hessian, solves subproblem nearly exactly eigendecomposition. robust, iteration costs O(n^3). steihaug() uses derivative-based model, solves subproblem approximately conjugate gradients (CG). CG stops early reaches trust-region boundary finds direction negative curvature. Hessian never factorized. supply Hessian-vector products (hessvec), Hessian never formed . bobyqa() newuoa() never use derivatives. fit quadratic model npt previously evaluated points (usually 2n + 1), take model’s remaining freedom smallest change Hessian. step found truncated CG, NEWUOA’s subproblem solver close spirit Steihaug’s; BOBYQA’s also respects box bounds. track two radii: rho, lower bound shrinks, rhobeg rhoend, controls termination; delta, step radius, can grow shrink .

code: cpp_code <- ' // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppTrust)]] #include <Rcpp.h> #include <vector>  extern "C" { #define iniRcppTrustPtrs _vignette2_iniRcppTrustPtrs #include <RcppTrust.h> iniRcppTrust }  // Derivative-free objective for NEWUOA. extern "C" int rosen_f(int n, const double *x, double *f, void *) {   double t = x[1] - x[0] * x[0];   *f = 100.0 * t * t + (1.0 - x[0]) * (1.0 - x[0]);   return 0; }  // Value/gradient on request, for Steihaug. The Hessian is never requested // in matrix-free mode. extern "C" int rosen_vg(int n, const double *x, double *value,                         double *gradient, double *hessian, void *) {   double t = x[1] - x[0] * x[0];   if (value) *value = 100.0 * t * t + (1.0 - x[0]) * (1.0 - x[0]);   if (gradient) {     gradient[0] = -400.0 * x[0] * t - 2.0 * (1.0 - x[0]);     gradient[1] = 200.0 * t;   }   return 0; }  extern "C" int rosen_hv(int n, const double *x, const double *v, double *hv,                         void *) {   double h11 = 1200.0 * x[0] * x[0] - 400.0 * x[1] + 2.0, h12 = -400.0 * x[0];   hv[0] = h11 * v[0] + h12 * v[1];   hv[1] = h12 * v[0] + 200.0 * v[1];   return 0; }  // [[Rcpp::export]] Rcpp::NumericMatrix fit_many(SEXP ptrTable, int nStarts) {   _vignette2_iniRcppTrustPtrs(ptrTable);  // normally done once in .onLoad()   Rcpp::NumericMatrix out(nStarts, 4);   std::vector<double> res(4 * nStarts);   // Build with OpenMP (e.g. -fopenmp in the package Makevars) to run   // this loop in parallel; without it the pragma is ignored.   #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(2)   for (int i = 0; i < nStarts; i++) {     double start[2] = {-1.2 + 0.05 * i, 1.0};      minqa_options_t mo = minqa_options_default(2, start);     minqa_result_t mr;     newuoa_solve_c_ptr(2, start, rosen_f, nullptr, &mo, &mr);      steihaug_options_t so = steihaug_options_default();     steihaug_result_t sr;     steihaug_solve_c_ptr(2, start, rosen_vg, rosen_hv, nullptr, &so, &sr);      res[4 * i] = mr.par[0];     res[4 * i + 1] = mr.feval;     res[4 * i + 2] = sr.argument[0];     res[4 * i + 3] = sr.iterations;     minqa_result_free_ptr(&mr);     steihaug_result_free_ptr(&sr);   }   for (int i = 0; i < nStarts; i++)     for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) out(i, j) = res[4 * i + j];   Rcpp::colnames(out) = Rcpp::CharacterVector::create(       "newuoa_x1", "newuoa_feval", "steihaug_x1", "steihaug_iter");   return out; } ' Rcpp::sourceCpp(code = cpp_code) head(fit_many(RcppTrust:::.RcppTrustPtr(), 16L)) #>      newuoa_x1 newuoa_feval steihaug_x1 steihaug_iter #> [1,] 0.9999998          257           1            27 #> [2,] 1.0000000          259           1            43 #> [3,] 0.9999999          262           1            36 #> [4,] 1.0000000          285           1            30 #> [5,] 0.9999996          282           1            29 #> [6,] 0.9999999          298           1            32

code: library(RcppTrust)  # Rosenbrock's function, the example from ?trust::trust objfun <- function(x) {   f <- expression(100 * (x2 - x1^2)^2 + (1 - x1)^2)   g1 <- D(f, "x1"); g2 <- D(f, "x2")   h11 <- D(g1, "x1"); h12 <- D(g1, "x2"); h22 <- D(g2, "x2")   x1 <- x[1]; x2 <- x[2]   list(     value = eval(f), gradient = c(eval(g1), eval(g2)),     hessian = rbind(c(eval(h11), eval(h12)), c(eval(h12), eval(h22)))   ) }  out <- trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5) out[c("value", "argument", "converged", "iterations")] #> $value #> [1] 5.165437e-15 #>  #> $argument #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 21

text: Every optimizer package implemented C-callable core R API calls global state, can run concurrently OpenMP/parallel C++ code (e.g. inner outer optimizer nlmixr2est). R functions [trust()], [steihaug()], [bobyqa()] [newuoa()] thin wrappers around cores.

what: Steihaug truncated-CG trust-region Newton minimization — steihaug
title: Steihaug truncated-CG trust-region Newton minimization — steihaug
text: Thread-safe C++ port trust-region Newton minimizer Steihaug truncated conjugate-gradient subproblem Rust crate basin (TrustRegion default Steihaug subproblem, driven basin's executor). iteration approximately minimizes quadratic model \(m(p) = f + g^T p + \frac{1}{2} p^T B p\) \(\|p\| \le \Delta\) conjugate gradients, stopping boundary negative curvature. Unlike [trust()] never factorizes Hessian, hessvec never forms (basin's matrix-free mode).

title: Steihaug truncated-CG trust-region Newton minimization — steihaug

code: fr <- function(x) 100 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)^2 + (1 - x[1])^2 grr <- function(x) c(-400 * x[1] * (x[2] - x[1]^2) - 2 * (1 - x[1]),                      200 * (x[2] - x[1]^2)) hr <- function(x) matrix(c(1200 * x[1]^2 - 400 * x[2] + 2, -400 * x[1],                            -400 * x[1], 200), 2, 2) steihaug(c(-1.2, 1), fr, grr, hr) #> $par #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $value #> [1] 8.628062e-25 #>  #> $gradient #> [1]  3.688916e-11 -1.851852e-11 #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 27 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $status #> [1] 4 #>  #> $message #> [1] "GradientTolerance" #>  #> $radius #> [1] 0.05108575 #>  #> $counts #>      fn      gr    hess hessvec  #>      31      28      27       0  #>   # matrix-free: only Hessian-vector products hv <- function(x, v) drop(hr(x) %*% v) steihaug(c(-1.2, 1), fr, grr, hessvec = hv)$counts #>      fn      gr    hess hessvec  #>      31      28       0      76

title: RcppTrust 0.2.0
text: package license now GPL-2, BOBYQA/NEWUOA ports R wrappers derive GPL-2 package ‘minqa’. M. J. D. Powell added author BOBYQA/NEWUOA algorithms original Fortran code; sources notices ported code (‘trust’, ‘basin’, ‘minqa’, Powell’s Fortran) listed inst/COPYRIGHTS. New steihaug(): Steihaug truncated conjugate-gradient trust-region Newton minimizer ported Rust crate ‘basin’, exact-Hessian matrix-free (Hessian-vector product) modes, thread-safe C entry point steihaug_solve_c(). New bobyqa() newuoa(): thread-safe C++ ports Powell’s derivative-free BOBYQA NEWUOA ‘minqa’ 1.2.8, drop-replacements minqa::bobyqa()/minqa::newuoa(), C entry points bobyqa_solve_c()/newuoa_solve_c(). BOBYQA’s RESCUE step evaluates intended point rather minqa’s uninitialized one. .RcppTrustPtr() RcppTrust.h gain appended slots new C entry points result-free functions. New vignette vignette("trust-region-methods").
